It has been a while since I've reminded you of this. This is important information, so I want to make sure you don't forget.

I even went an extra step this time. This is pretty close to the recipe I generally use, though I make mine in larger batches and don't do any of that sifting crap or similar. I just chuck the ingredients in the bowl.

https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/21014/good-old-fashioned-pancakes/

I also use less sugar and often use a mix of cream and whole milk. Think of the recipe as a starting point, and not a finishing point. They're pancakes and you don't need no stinkin' rules.

Anyhow, from there, I often mix in fruit - but not when I make the batter. I usually make the batter in large batches and add the fruit later. You can store pancake batter quite easily, and it survives being frozen just fine.

They're pancakes - meaning you can do anything you want with them. You can even use canned fruit, draining the juice off before adding it to the batter. Frozen fruit works just fine. They're pancakes, so the sky is pretty much the limit.

That recipe is a good starting point. You can try different flour types, for example. If you ran out of regular sugar, you can even use confectioner's sugar but probably want to use less. (Trust me on this one, I've been there before and used to be pretty poor so I didn't have regular sugar.) Brown sugar works fine and you can even make them without sugar.

If eggs are a problem, you can substitute an equal volume of yogurt.

The baking powder matters. I'm not sure why, but the pancakes don't come out nearly as well if you skip that. Not gonna lie, I don't even know what the baking powder does. I just know that they are thick without the baking powder, to the point where they're too thick. My understanding is that the powder releases CO2, but I have no idea how. I guess that makes 'em lighter. So, don't forget to add some. As near as I can tell, it's just got to be an approximate amount.

If Putt ever fixes the formatting, I may try typing out some more pancake recipes. For example, cornmeal pancakes are delicious.
